title: Episode 8: The Wasted Opportunity
review:
At first, I didn't want to write this review, but this movie was such an injustice to the franchise that I couldn't hold back any longer. Before I continue, yes, as a fan, I had expectations, but those expectations were fanned by the lore created in TFA. If you didn't want the fans to have expectations regarding certain elements, which I will cover in this review, than you shouldn't have created the lore responsible for said expectations. We were given so much possibility for potential growth and Johnson destroyed all of it. For the sake of this review, I will only cover a few major issue I had with TLJ. I will not be covering Luke Skywalker cause as much as I didn't like his direction, it did match similar Jedi in the past like Ulic Qel-Droma (Redemption) and Jedi Master Lucien (KOTOR).

1. Snoke: In TFA, we are presented with a mysterious figure who is extremely powerful and yet he is not a Sith Lord. He has scars all over his face and what appears to be a saber slash. We know almost nothing about the origins of this dark figure or the methods he will use to complete Kylo Ren's training and thanks to Johnson, you'll never know. Despite how TFA ended, Kyle Ren is given zero training and Snoke is killed without any further development of his character. What could have been one of the most fascinating characters was turned into a 2 dimensional villain. How exciting!...

2. Rey: I loved Rey as a new character and her development was awesome. I felt she was a refreshing change for Star Wars and a symbol for young girls that even they can be heroes. She had an interesting lore regarding her mysterious connection to her force as well as who she was related to. Additionally, TFA set viewers up with all kinds of exciting possibilities regarding her training with Luke as well as her relationship with Finn. However, TLJ gives us barely any training time with Luke, her parents are literally nobodies and her natural connection to the force exists simply because? I understand that this portrayal of showing the world how even the underdog can be awesome was their intended direction after watching the film, but this idea has been done to death! Rey's origin story was completely underwhelming and left me feeling disappointed.

3. Leia: I know that Leia has a connection to the force based on what Luke said in ROTJ, but we are given absolutely zero explanation to how she used such advanced force techniques to save her life in the vacuum of space. Yes, it's been 30-40 years since ROTJ, but the books made it clear Leia was busy dealing with the New Republic where she then created the Resistance to salvage what ships she could since the New Republic was destroying all of the militaristic devices. So when did she has time to learn the techniques she used to save her life? At least have a voice over from Luke to establish she learned something from him. Instead, she conveniently has the ability to save her life in an impossible situation simply because.

4. Kylo Ren: As much as some people loved his character, still trying to understand why, Kylo Ren was just as whiny if not even more emotionally annoying than before. His character just seems to be there. He doesn't continue his training and whenever he tries to be terrifying, people just laughed. It's okay to add comedy, but Star Wars needs to be taken a little more seriously. Look at TESB, there was organic comedy that made the characters lovable. That being said, every evil character was dark, terrifying, and powerful. Their presence was memorable and redefined the presence of darkness. Whenever Kylo Ren threw someone, people just cackled which shouldn't be the reaction a dark lord gets.

5. Rose: I can't even say that name without getting angry. Her character was completely useless and a clear plug. According to Disney, she was a step forward for the Star Wars franchise because she's an Asian woman. How is this a step forward?! We already had several Asian leads, 2 of which were from Rogue one and they were amazing! We also had a female Asian Jedi Knight in TCW colosseum fight scene. Plus! We already have had several amazing female leads! So how is she a step forward?! *takes a breath* Furthermore, her character background is overly simplistic. She comes from hardship and slavery under the rule of the First Order. Because this idea of hardship has never been done before right? Then, after only knowing Finn, in person, for maybe 12 hours, she says she loves him?! Come on Disney! at least make your romance believable in a Star Wars film. Now some people defend her purpose in the film because she saved Finn's life, but had Luke never shown up to save the Resistance, the drill would have destroyed the door and the First Order would have killed everyone, which includes Finn. The reality is Rose was just a star struck emotional horny teeny bopper that wanted to get some and she didn't care about anyone else. Her character, as a whole, was annoying and pointless. She some how made Jar Jar look good and that's a terrible achievement.

I could say more, but these are my major beefs with TLJ. The reality is this movie focused on new characters that were either useless or boring and gave zero respect to the lore created in TFA. It's a disgrace to Star Wars and a movie I assure you will only be remembered as the worst Star Wars movie of all time.

title: The movie was a disappointment, and unintelligent.
review:
The positive reviews will try to convince you that a flip flopping storyline like this is Super intelligent, and is thought provoking.

However, I am here to say that it feels more like the director rolled dice to see what would happen. Almost every time they set up something to happen, the next scene cuts itself short. Not once in this movie was there any payoff.

Characters go on quests, fight, and die for what seems like a pointless waste of time. The set up character arcs that are never advanced, and others never needed to exist. Some of the characters just a few days after episode 7 seem to suddenly be masters of subjects they know nothing about. Finn can now pilot with no training, and Rey can do everything she needs to with the force without any effort. Rey didn't even learn anything from Luke.

Now I'm not saying its necessarily a bad thing that Rey is more powerful than Luke, but does he really have to not teach her anything? Where is the Wise Luke we knew from Return of The Jedi? Why the hell would he turn a Saber on his sleeping nephew? (his best friend's and his sister's son.) Luke was the guy who risked everything for the second most evil man in the galaxy, his Father. like WTF?

Many people have been waiting to see this character again for 30+ years, and this is what you give them?

Sure I can understand that Disney didn't want the old characters to get in the way of the new heroes, but there were so many other ways to handle Lukes character that didn't require him to be a Grumpy old man who gave up on his family and friends, and spent at least a decade on an Island alone because he wanted to die.

Some would say that he wanted to die because of what he did to Ben Solo, but I would argue that Luke would never have done that in the first place. Even if he did, he would have done his best to make things right over the years.

Star Wars used to be about the bond between family and friends, and how important those bonds are. Now its about how people are losers, how they become losers, and how some losers are sometimes cowards too. Its about how people are two faced, stupid, and secretive towards their second in command. Its about how important it is to follow leadership blindly. Its about almost killing the one you love, instead of self sacrifice for you friends. Its about the mistreated race horses, and not the slave children. Its about how stupid evil people are, and about how violence is the right answer to everything (talking about how Rey responds to every doubt of hers). Its about how nobody needs to put in effort because when someone else does the work for you, you get better grades. Its about killing the old Star Wars, because you know the fans won't let it die.

While this movie has great special effects, it is boring, flip flopping, uninspired and outright disrespectful to the previous heroes of the story. The director had no idea about what story he was trying to portray, and so he took everything set up by the previous movie, and answered them in the easiest way possible, left them out entirely, or killed them off before you could get an answer. The force now feels more like Dungeons and Dragon's magic, instead of how mythical and faith based it was in the previous movies.

When you use a character whose arc is complete, like Luke, there is no need to reset them to square one. You can let them pass on their knowledge, and blessing to the new heroes instead.

when you have a series of movies with a huge fan-base, the fan-base has certain expectations from that series. When you betray the core of it, of course people are gonna be upset. This movie does just that. Betrayed our trust. Tried to be something it never was, nor was ever meant to be, and lost its life in the process.

What a disappointment.

title: Marginally Better than the Prequels
review:
It was going to be difficult to please everybody and in the end this movie ended pleasing very few people instead.

The thing that made The Force Awakens so enjoyable was that it was able to re-connect Star Wars fans with many of the things that made them have an emotional connection with the original trilogy. The realignment was sorely needed after the dismal prequel trilogy. Yes, there were fan service call backs and the familiar plot of blowing up a death star. But, it worked. Abrams is very good at playing in other creator's sandboxes... moving the pieces around, making them fit, telling new stories while keeping the elements familiar.

That went out the window with The Last Jedi. I was initially very excited to see what Johnson would do with the story now that the table had been set. In some ways he does a very respectable job moving the entire narrative along. However, he does this at the expense of the original characters.

This treatment of Luke is perhaps the most universally derided part of the movie and for good reason. Luke Skywalker is a hero to so many people. To portray him as a weird hermit and failed Jedi is an affront to many Star War's fan's core beliefs. Yes, I get that people may become jaded with time or that occasionally challenging an audience's perception of a character can be a useful story telling device. However, Johnson took it too far and this leaves Luke's long awaited appearance wholly unfulfilling. The notion that he'd kill his nephew is completely at odds with everything we know about him.

Leia's 'space walk' moment, or whatever you care to call it, was a cheap ploy that immediately takes you out of the movie. I feel that this unnecessarily toys with the audience especially in light of Carrie Fisher's passing.

Now, I was shocked and appalled when 'fans' pitched a fit over the casting of Daisy Ridley and John Boyega for TFA. The level of racist and misogyny commentary was horrible considering what this story is supposed to be about. However, I feel that Disney has crossed a threshold and is now trying to shoe-horn in strong female and minority characters where ever and whenever possible. This is especially ironic after they've spent the last 70 years making money off the whole 'Disney Princess' convention which has now fallen out of vogue. I love Daisy Ridley's character. However, the A-wing pilot, Admiral Holdo, and the Tico sisters are wholly unnecessary and this line of discourse plays out in the whole casino story line. It took Star Wars 40 years to finally introduce a character of Asian origin and the best you can do is Rose Tico? Look, she's not as bad as Jar Jar by half, but she's not much better. I really hope that this character becomes something meaningful in episode 9.

Its my option that truly great movies are able to subtly touch and reflect on current events. This movie, instead, hamfistedly says eating Porgs are bad (vegetarianism), income equality is bad (slave labor and the excesses of the 1%), using animals for entertainment is bad (Fathier racing), through the DJ character that choosing sides is bad (so let's all be mercenaries). While these are not necessarily plot points they are obvious, persistent, and irritating.

Finally, before I finish, I do have one good thing to say. Although its far too little and way too late the final scene of the movie reminds us what much of this franchise has been about. It reminds us that greatness can come from anywhere (Luke, after all, was just a farm boy and his father a slave). I think that this final scene is timely and is something that all Star Wars fans can connect with. We all believe that there's something great in us, some latent ability that can propel us to achieve great things. Its finally an admittance that there is no 'chose one' as Anakin was prophesied to be but rather a realization that great things can only be accomplished by many people working together. Its the one note that The Last Jedi correctly hits.

In sum, I don't think Rian Johnson really understood the world in which he was working and it shows. The movie has its moments but will serve as a dividing point in the fan base for years to come (unless it gets the Highland II treatment). Now, Rian Johnson doesn't care about this, he's been paid. But the rest of the fan base will either have to reconcile their differences with the movie, or choose to ignore it like I ignore Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull. It's also damning that the supposed Blue-ray version will have an additional 20 mins pushing the run time to nearly 3 hours. In the end Johnson didn't understand the sand box in which he was playing and instead of telling a Star Wars story he simply missed the mark and told a bad one.

title: I wish I could unsee it
review:
I never thought I would say this to a Star Wars movie, but seriously, people, DON'T PAY FOR THIS PIECE OF BANTHA DUNG. I had such high hopes after The Force Awakens, since it was not perfect, but it felt like a new beginning of a brand new Star Wars adventure with interesting characters and a good storyline. But after The last Jedi, I felt like I got a spit in the face. I won't write down that huge pile of mistakes in the movie, because a lot of commenters said it already, but this movie is a big shame not only for the Star Wars universe, but for the movie industry as well. If Disney can sell such an incomplete, boring movie with the worst script ever just because of the good CGI and a few cute aliens, then our whole society truly should reconsider its values. I'm utterly disappointed, sad and angry at the same time and can't understand those people (yes, there is a LOT) who actually liked this movie. Did you watch something else? Did I watch some parody by mistake? What on Earth could you people like in this AT ALL? 
Yes, the movie had some good-looking scenes and of course the music was amazing, that's the only reason it could deserve 2 stars at most... But those stars go only for John Williams and the digital effects crew. 
All in all, I regret paying for it. I regret wasting 2 and a half hours of my life. I regret ruining the whole Star Wars sensation in myself. 
Seriously... I wish I could unsee it...

title: Terrible direction and writing, wrecks what might one day be a good Episode 8
review:
I went to see this today, curious as to how it could be possible for so many film review sites and publications to rate the film so highly, and yet so, so many actual viewers rate it so badly.

I simply could not believe that Disney could have 'bought off' so many hundreds of magazines and sites (including this one)- after all, if thats possible, why didn't Warner Bros do the same thing with Justice League?

But I'm afraid to say there seems to be no other logical explaination.

The reviews I read from the likes of Empire and so on, spoke about how moving and thrilling the film was. Twitter was alive with people saying they were shaking with excitement and shock and so on.

I honestly think you would have to have serious mental problems to have that kind of reaction to this drawn out, heartless, often cringe-worthy movie.

Sorry to say it, because I wish I didn't agree, and had enjoyed the film more myself, but the overwhelming mass of reviews on this site, that did not like the film, are right.

It does not in the slightest, channel 'Empire Strikes Back', it has much, much more in common with 'The Phantom Menace' particularly in its ill judged attempts at 'humour' that are about on a par with Jar-Jar Binks.

And it suffers from the same key problem that did, terrible direction.

That became totally clear when the first credit shows at the end, 'Written and Directed by Rian Johnson'. Almost everything else wrong with the film could be overlooked, if the writing and direction were not so awful.

Right from the start, we are subject to Johnsons so called humour, and whether its your brand of humour or not, there is no escaping the fact that he relentlessly makes characters do things they *simply would not do*.

Very early in the film Rey hands Skywalker her sabre, to swelling music, asking him to train her in the ways of the force. Skywalker chucks it over his shoulder and walks off. We are supposed to fall about the place laughing, but we just cringe, because there is simply no way Luke would do that.

And that sort of rubbish, happens non-stop through the film, destroying almost every moment of drama, emotion or tension, shaking you out of the story, removing every trace of any feeling of 'epicness' this 'space opera' should have and subjecting us again and again to Johnsons, inane, insensitive, childish attempts to make us laugh.

StarWars never was 'funny' per se. But it had funny moments and these came about not from some forced directoral 'cheap gags' but from the characters. Han Solo was a wize cracking, cynical, rogue, and therefore he said things that were funny sometimes, but always the comic moments were believable as things those characters might *actually do or say*

The other big issue is that its far too long, but again this smacks of poor direction to me. The film just feels like it desperately needed a decent editor to tighten it up, give it the pace and drama it deserves, but that Johnson just would not let it happen, couldn't get rid of all the 'good bits' he added.

The light at the end of the tunnel, is that most of the garbage *can* probably be edited out by fans. So once the DVD comes out keep your eyes peeled on fanedit.org for a better version. There are edits on there that even make 'The Phantom Menace' almost decent.

title: Star Wars doesn't want or need me anymore.
review:
I've not used IMDB to write a review in a few years now, but after viewing Star Wars: The Last Jedi recently, I decided to return to the fold. Straight to the point I was very disappointed with this entry in a number of areas, but there were things in it I enjoyed, hence the five stars.

I understand and agree that Star Wars has to evolve to survive and prosper in the 21st century and I appreciate that some of the decisions taken with regards to plot and character in the new film reflect this ethos. I knew this going in with the previous film, old favourites were going to "retire", new characters were going to come to the fore, perfectly reasonable.

What I couldn't prepare myself for, was the conspicuous inclusion of real world politics and social issues. I've never questioned these elements in other entertainments. Even populist stuff, can be a good forum to deal with subjects in an indirect way.

That said, I felt that I was being lectured by this film, as though they felt that to entertain me for my £19:95 was secondary to it telling me how much Women Contribute to our society, the inherent bad points that Men have, how certain cultures are exploited for profit by others.

As I said, some of the issues above I mention are worthy and deserve to be addressed, but not with such a heavy hand or so frequently, and not when I've simply gone to some expense to enjoy a couple of hours of escapist fun. I felt as though I was drip fed the things I wanted, in between lectures. Star Wars has tried to parallel our real world before, certainly in George Lucas's desire to symbolize the Vietnam conflict in Return of the Jedi's climatic battle between the low tech Ewoks and the highly technological Empire. That said, it was implied, but not over implied, you never felt patronised. I don't resent the presence of modern tropes, just they're prevalence, consequently this is the least favourite Star Wars experience I have ever had since the age of 7 in 1977. Actual plot wise, I also feel that it is weak storytelling to present your audience with Anakin's light sabre, hidden in a wooden box in the backroom of a space bar, in the previous instalment, surely unrecoverable from where it was lost, only to have the mystery of it's recovery reduced to an over the shoulder site gag in the next film. What happened with Snoke was surprising, but I can accept it, as having another Emporer like figure draws unfavourable comparison and is therefore reductive. I felt that Rose and Finn's story was a little mute and the inclusion of the prosperous Casino planet was a strategically placed element to engender some subtle and not so subtle social commentary.

There is no equality in diminishing others, the new films are growing more guilty of this as they progress. Not just men having to be critiqued in order to elevate women, but the original trilogy diminished in its victories, which I feel betrays a lack of confidence in Star Wars' new owners that they have any tricks up their sleeves comparable to the quality of the original films.

I have struggled with the notion that Return of the Jedi wasn't quite the victory it seemed, Han and Leia had a failed marriage, Luke lost his way and became embittered, it stings, to a fan, particularly one who waited patiently since 1983 to find out what happened next. I just cannot except that the boy who grew to manhood fighting an evil, galaxy spanning Empire, forsaking his birth right for his friends and nearly sacrificing all to redeem his father. Would consider the murder of his nephew in his sleep and then give up entirely in the aftermath and withdraw to die in exile. A character as optimistic, hopeful and frankly, as good previously, is viewed with more than a pinch of derision and cynicism in our new century. Luke, as he was, is unpalatable to the new generation, characters previously like Luke, are now, particularly the men, anguished, indecisive, hopeless. The disappointment isn't really Luke's though, but those of society at large he now returns to, projecting it's own disillusionment, anguish and hopelessness onto a paragon from a simpler, happier time. Just a thought.

I grow truly weary of properties being resurrected from my childhood, only to discover their form is unwelcome and a "bad fit" for modern sensibilities, consequently becoming mangled and contorted, as lesser hands try to make them fit into a culture which has moved on. I feel that Star Wars is no longer for me or me for it, it doesn't want my support or seek my approval, maybe this is the clean break we needed, it can go on and impress new people and I can stay at home with my blu rays, sulk and eat chocolate. I never thought I'd write these things about Star Wars, feel this alienated by it, maybe it was inevitable or maybe some have tried to push it a little too quickly into the 21st century, we'll see with the next one.

review:
I won't waste my time writing a detailed review, you can find some excellent ones on this forum.

title: i hope everyone now realises how good George Lucas was!
review:
I give it 5 stars, there is half a good movie here. Great visuals. And of course, an amazing soundtrack.

I love the 6 film cycle because it is one true story from one man's vision (and hundreds of great artists). But it is now clear that, despite the fun of The Force Awakens, there is no planned-out continuing story for this sequel trilogy. What a shame we don't get to see George Lucas's sequel triology. But people attacked him and complained about the prequels.

I don't normally write reviews, but I felt obliged too here and on Rotten Tomatoes, because the ratings seem way to high, and most revoiws I am reading from fans are negative. Most general audience people I know and have read, are happy with the movie, like I would happy with a Marvel movie. But anyone who is emotionally attached to Star Wars is probably going to come out of this movie feeling empty and disappointed; much more so than the Phantom Menace. Episode 1, which i think is the weakest, is pretty dull and boring in many places, but it is still part of an epic story.

title: What you did with Luke's character is completely unbelievable!
review: The director's efforts to shake things up and make something new aside, the twisting of Luke Skywalker's character is unforgivable. That the man who would never give up on the light inside Darth Vader, who being the chosen one with countless deaths on his shoulders would have a far deeper and more powerful darkness inside him then a budding Ben Solo would, would go to confront Ben, at night, carrying a light saber, while Ben slept, is preposterous! He would have gone calmly, with love and light in his heart, and a determination to bring Ben to the light (as he did with his father). Everything else that was done with Luke's character was based on a behavior that he would never in a million years engaged in! I have never been more disappointed in my life with a plot-line or a director's handling of a character. And he has effectively taken away any chance that those of us who waited 30+ years to see the awesomeness of what Luke represented and had become would look like. Disgusting...

title: Much below my expectations
review:
The main issue of this movie is the storyline: it's really trivial and has so many holes it's difficult to make sense of it. I was definitely not pleased with the role of Luke, nor with Snoke's or Kylo's. It really seems to me that whoever came up with the story either did not care much or deeply misunderstood the saga. The humour is out of place, and characters are underdeveloped.
It's really a shame the saga was mistreated this way.

title: Not Much Else To Say
review: Not much else to say that hasn't already been said. Just wanted to add my vote to the chorus of criticism for this movie. The plot feels completely inconsistent with both The Force Awakens (which I really enjoyed), the original trilogy, and even within just this movie itself. It jumps around from scene to scene like an action flick without any substance. The casino scene was completely unnecessary and seemingly major characters are revealed to be almost entirely unimportant - including, most surprisingly, Luke Skywalker. Thumbs down.

title: Disappointing.....devoid of feeling, passion and just about everything else that is Star Wars!
review:
I will try to keep my comment unique to my experience and make one comment regarding a majority of the other reviews regarding the writer of this series. Yes Disney has pimped out the saga to the whims of writers who do not embody the true spirit of the Star Wars saga and the fans who have made it successful all these years. I was disgusted and left the theater when Leia and Vice Admiral Holdo mock the hallmark of Star Wars, "May the force be with you...always!", by laughing about it when they say it at the same time. Reckless and unacceptable in any context and disrespectful to the Saga and the fans who made Star Wars what it is today. And to the writer....anybody can plagiarize a script by putting the plot of A New Hope, Return of the Jedi and the Empire Strikes back in one movie. Please do us a favor and write yourself out of the script like Han Solo or Luke Skywalker since it obvious you are resentful against what made Star Wars successful. 
I will save the spoilers however if the plot can be summed up as such. Start at the end of Return of the Jedi with the big battle (except the hero is demoted for his heroism and the battle between Darth Vader and Luke - Kylo Ren and Rey is moved further into the plot) with a chase ensuing ala the beginning of a New Hope, then jump back to Rey training with Luke like Luke and Yoda Empire Strikes Back Style, Fin and Rose try to deactivate the tracking system like deactivating the force shield in either A New Hope or Return of the Jedi while Kylo Ren and Rey figure it out like Return of the Jedi ending in a battle and escaping like the Hoth battle scene from Empire Strikes Back. In the mean time we kill off another leading male role Luke Sky Walker, man what a pile of crap!
The movie lacks feeling, depth, humility, purpose or compassion and is just straight up devoid of emotion. This movie does not move me at all except to leave the theatre.

review:

The directors have changed if people didn't know. That is why the movie was totally different. I don't agree with changing directors during a sequel or there should've been some guidelines made. Start your own saga or version of Star Wars. The company did horrible allowing him to make such drastic changes...We should all protest about how they offended Star Wars! Never watch anymore movies related to Star Wars.

title: Star Wars: It's the Longest One
review:
How does DJ know the rebel's plan? Finn and Rose don't know the plan (and why would they have told him if they did know?), Poe doesn't know the plan and this is all established in the previous scene but somehow DJ sells information that he can't possibly have to the First Order.

Luke is going to burn down a tree with Jedi books in it, pauses for a minute and is then upset when Yoda burns down the tree... Why?

The whole movie is just the laziest writing. They are going to run out of fuel but they are also just fast enough to stay out of range of the First Order ships.

I don't feel like this movie is really bad, it's just disappointing. This movie is style over substance. It's difficult to believe that everyone at Disney read this script and thought it was great.

And none of the jokes are funny.

title: The Last Jedi or the shadow of Luke Skywalker or the end of Star Wars!
review:
What does a Star Wars movie separate from any other Sci-fi or fantasy movie? Star Wars has space battles, lightsaber duels, stormtroopers, action scenes and blaster duels. These are the optical things you expect in these movies and to some extent they are also there in The Last Jedi. Still there are also deeper meanings in Star Wars movies like the heart of friendship, sympathetic characters you can identify with, western and eastern mythology, the fight between good and evil and overcoming all obstacles. These are the things this new movie fails miserable and I start with the biggest failure, the characterization of Luke Skywalker.

We followed Luke from the naïve farmboy in A new Hope over his struggle to find his place in Empire strikes back to a matured warrior in Return of the Jedi. This was not even everything Luke showed us in the last OT movie, he even showed us forgiveness and humanity in the face of pure evil, when he did throw away his weapon and trusted his father to return to light and save him. It worked out and they celebrated the victory in Return of the Jedi.

Now 30 years later we finally learn Luke failed in everything from this point on. He failed to teach his sister (from Yoda :"pass on what you have learned") and Leia is not a Jedi. He tried it with some students and one was his nephew and prime student. But out of a sudden he enters his nephews room in the night and ignites his weapon to kill him, because he sensed some darkness in him. The his nephew awakes and it marks the creation of Kylo Ren.....what....who is this guy called Luke Skywalker in this movie? For sure not the same character we saw 30 years ago. Yes, characters can change over time, but it has to be a natural development and nothing is natural with a 180° turn, except lazy storytelling. Luke is used to create this strange Kylo&Rey force connection. As Mark Hamill said, he played Jake Skywalker instead of Luke Skywalker!

Now we come to the next big disappointment, Rey. Luke&Rey were expected to be the beating heart of the movie according to marketing, but what did we get? Grumpy, angry and broken Luke who wanted Rey to leave, that's the Luke&Rey plot as a whole. The scene between Luke&R2 was even the best scene of this movie and it showed a glimpse of the old known Luke. After this Luke agreed to train Rey a little, but was this really training? He acted like a senior primary school teacher when Rey reached out to the force. Ok, this was one of the failed comedy attempts. Rey continued like in The Force Awakens and she doesn't need a teacher, because she already knows everything, has no flaws, can use the force whenever she needs it, does not struggle with anything etc. There is even a scene in which Luke&Rey fight, after she thinks Luke is the bad guy and in this one Rey beats the Jedi master Luke (yeah one of the points where nothing did surprise me anymore). What did we learn about the force in this move? Hmmm, nothing really, only that it does not belong to the Jedi and so Luke decided to die on this island....what? (the visual dictionary goes even deeper and says Luke wants to do a final Jedi rite = suicide?).

We come to another big issue of this movie, the failed humor (or Marvel humor entering Star Wars). The movie itself started good with Poe attacking in his X-Wing the First Order to help the resitance escaping. But already 5 minutes into this movie, this misplaced humor started when Poe made a prank call to Hux. Never make the bad guys the object of slapstick humor unless you make a parody ala 'Spaceballs'. Hux was later more victim of more comedy when he was ridiculed by Snoke in front of the other soldiers. Luke was partly used in such a way too, when he did just throw the lightsaber over his shoulder, after one movie before was build up to this big moment of Rey handing Luke the lightsaber.....what? It was for nothing. Then we saw some of Luke's daily life and I wish I could get the scene out of my head with Luke milking this big pace creature for green milk....please noooooo. We also got a scene in which Luke wants to burn the temple tree after Rey was gone, but cannot do it and then Yoda appears and shows him that he did not learn anything in 30 years, because Yoda is still the master and force lightning style burns the tree...what?

After we already learned that we have again super Rey, so what about the other new characters? Finn, he is again used for comedy and lead together with another useless character, Rose, a mission that accomplished nothing.....what? They spend around 30 -40 minutes for a plot to get a codebreaker on a casino planet and freed some animals, but the mission as a whole was a failure. So we have Poe and the new leader Holdo (after Leia was out in coma for some time) and we get a dynamic of one soldier not blindly obeying another soldier...so far fine, but this made no sense and Holdo could have just told Poe the real plan, which had saved us the useless Finn&Rose mission. But so we got a stupid Poe, because he could not sense this great plan....One thing I forgot was Leia, she was again sparely used and in one scene she used the force to save herself. So she was blown out in space after an attack and used the force to survive in space and to he worse, she flies back like Superman or Marry Poppins to safety. Then she falls in coma....(ok at that point nothing in this movie I was like, whatever).

Let us come to the final stand on a left former mineral planet rebel base. So Finn, Rose and some other survived soldiers tried to attack a big canon who could destroy the base and Finn was about to sacrifice himself to save everyone, but.....yeah....(weird Rian Johnson twist)....and Rose takes his ship down with her own to get a kiss from Finn. So the canon still exists and this means big entry for the last one who could do anything (maybe)...Luke. He has a little emotional scene with Leia and they both agree that Luke has to stop Kylo. Fine, so Luke confronts Kylo and his soldiers and nothing can hurt Luke. Finally we get the Luke we have been waiting for since 1983...(wait until the movie is over, it is a Rian movie). Then Kylo enters to face Luke in a lightsaber duel and wow, it gets better. Luke is doing it Matrix style (and got a hair cut + hair dye before). Now it looks like Luke sacrifices himself like Obi-Wan and we learn Luke was just a projection, while he still meditates on his island. Wow...impressive ...(wait until the movie is over, it is a Rian movie)...and a second later Luke falls down on his meditating rock, crawls, has a face of pain and finally fades away....yes, Luke Skywalker died of exhaustion!!!

But the movie ends with super Rey who saved some old books from the first temple, saves the surving soldiers by levitating rocks and we a slave boy who plays with a Luke Skywalker figure at the end and force grabs a broom....so the Disney future is saved....but the Star Wars future died with this movie. Who wants to see super Rey versus whining Kylo the 3rd encounter in episode IX? title: Guardians of the Fury Road Galactica
review:
The first couple of minutes set up the tone for the rest of the movie.

First of all, it established the mighty Imperial general as an ineffectual idiot who has problems even grasping the concept of microphones.

Secondly, if you though stormtroopers were horrible at aiming, just wait until you see the Imperial fleet. If one single fighter plane is able to take out every single gun of an entire battle cruiser, it makes the Empire look like the Keystone Cops and in no way a credible threat to the rebellion (which is further emphasized by their General being a pouty kid). One wonders why the rebellion even bothers to amass an armada when apparently one fighter per battle is all you need.

And finally we learn that this movie will be jam packed with lame attempts at comedy. It's obvious that someone at Disney has watched Guardians of the Galaxy far too many times.

The main storyline with the armada on the run going straight forward was the slowest and least exciting chase sequence since OJ Simpson's failed attempt at a getaway.

OK, let's buy that their ships were able to go slightly faster than the Imperial ships. Was there any reason for the Empire to not call for backup? The chase sequence lasts at least 16 hours in their universe, and in that time Finn and Rose are able to go to one planet, be imprisoned and escape, and get back to the armada. One would think that the Empire would be able to scramble some backup from another system in that time.

Or how about having half the Imperial fleet on site use their hyperdrive to get in front of the rebellion armada? Or, since were in three dimensional space, jump some of their ships in front of, below, above and to the side of the rebellion armada, attacking them from all sides?

If Luke Skywalker didn't want to be found and ran away to the most desolate place in the universe and have nothing to do with the rebellion, one can only wonder why he left a map to his whereabouts in the last movie.

The Finn and Rose storyline is completely meaningless as it changes nothing and has no impact on the story. Finn came close to serving a purpose in this movie when he was about to sacrifice himself, just to have his idiot new friend and love interest (apparently) smash into his speeder, cementing his role in this story as utterly useless.

I have loved Star Wars ever since I was a kid, and I watched this in the cinema with my girlfriend who couldn't care less about Star Wars. Interestingly enough we both laughed out loud at Rose's dying (?) words about the rebellion being about love or some bullsh*t, as those words came right after she had doomed all her friends and the entire rebellion to an apparently certain death through her kamikaze decision.

Rey is a Mary Sue once again, effortlessly holding her own against the Supreme Leader's elite body guard without prior training except shadowboxing against a rock for five minutes.

At the end of the movie (almost) all of the characters are back to where they started, having learned nothing but to blindly bow down to authority, apparently. Some rebels they are.

This movie took a huge, steaming dump all over the Star Wars legacy. Apparently the force and the Jedi mean nothing anymore in the Star Wars universe, rendering all previous movies meaningless. I wasn't a big fan of The Force awakens, but that movie almost seems like a masterpiece in retrospect.

In a way it's impressive that the prequel movies aren't the worst in the series anymore. This movie is the embodiment of midichlorians.

title: Worse than I imagined, instant sequel not worth seeing
review:
I was wondering whether the torrent of terrible reviews was some type of trickery because so many critics claimed to have loved this film. My first thought when it ended was "what the hell did I just watch?" Without spoiling the film, here's a list of everything why this film was such a clunker.

1) If you've ever watched the first 3 films that started this story, you have to wonder whether the writers ever did. The personalities simply don't match.

2) There are so many "wink wink" nod to the past film moments that it becomes laughable, making you wonder whether they ran out of money and the writers just said "aw hell, let's just recreate the same scenes and some of the dialog from prior films! Fans will love it!" Ummm.... no. It's contrived.

3) Many of the numerous jokey scenes fall flat on their butts.

4) Far fetched escapes is suspending disbelief. This film has repeated miracle moments and made for drama. Must totally disconnect brain for this film. Entirely.

5) The rules of the force and logic are broken repeatedly. Stuff happens when it does because it needs to. And it's obvious.

6) The ending of the movie, which I won't give away, is simply made for a sequel. And it ends the way it does because, if it didn't, they'd have to figure out a whole new sequel and excuse to keep this rubbish afloat.

7) I now understand why Mark Hamil was so outspoken about this film with criticism over treatment of Skywalker. It was hilariously bad and pitiful. The word "lame" has been redefined. They could have had the story go in hundreds of different directions. This one felt like they couldn't figure one out so they chose the one that took the least effort.

8) I don't know whether the director wants to promote some type of romantic connection between these new young lead characters. It seems like Rian Johnson wasn't sure either. And let me tell you that what they've got feels ice cold.

9) I disagree that casting a woman as a Jedi was a bad or forced idea.Daisy Ridley does a great job given what she was given. She might be the only thing half keeping the movie together. But ultimately there is really nothing behind all the mumbo jumbo. And as the film goes on, you realize that her job is to sound strong, act cool and be a good baddie. I'm not sure what she really does.

10) Either characters were written into the script to do someone a favor (Benicio Del Toro) or this has to be the laziest job of script writing I've seen in a long time. You could see certain plot points happen from a mile away. You almost wanted to scream at the characters in the film about what you're seeing as the audience. That's not a good place to be.

There is a lot more I could say about this film and the best I can say is that the visuals make this film look beautiful. But it is a painful watch. There is only one thing for sure. This is the last Jedi as you've known it. It seems like Rian Johnson wants to take this brand in a different direction but now it's as generic as any other space war film. I think too many of the critics didn't want to anger Disney too much with a bad review, which is why you saw a ridiculous number of laudatory reviews.

title: Do or do not. There is no try.
review:
Got very mixed feelings about this. I'll just adress the parts That gave a disturbance in the force:
Snokes death: pros: he was never that intriguing to me anyways. His arrogance killed him much like it was the case with Palpatine. Cons: regardless of him being a stereotypical uber villain, he did seem to fill the part of main opponent, since Kylo Ren seems more like a study in angst. With Snoke, starkiller base and Snokes flag ship out of the game I have difficulty seeing the typical sense of things to take care of for our heroes in episode 9. 
Lukes death: pros: Actually liked the grumpy old man approach... cons: But spending Lukes life the way it was done seemed utter wastefull, regarding 35 years speculating what he'd be able to do as an old jedi master. It was, to me, a lack of ideas that made them spend him in an attempt to mirror Yodas serene death i RotJ. 
Hyperspace kamikaze: pros: looked cool. Cons: it changed the "rules" of all future space battles in Star Wars... The next time the rebel fleet is hopelessly outnumbered, hyperspace kamikaze as an option seems required. 
Reys family background: pros: Anakin came from humble beginnings also. Cons: dont serve up mysteries and then kill then so backhandedly as it was done. 
The gambling planet detour: pros: none. Cons: overall this side plot served no purpose at all other than screen time for main characters, introduction of benicios character which I didnt come to care for anyways and his final betrayel as a result was so anticlimactic. 
Captain Phasma: Again a totally wasted character... She be "killed a third time" in episode 9, as I cant imagine that falling into flames present her bigger difficulties escaping than being locked in a trash conpacter on an exploding superweapon. 
All in all this movie reeked of a director not liking the setup given to him from episode 7, and thus disposing of same for cheap surprizes rather than working with it.

title: Star Wars: The Rian Menace
review:
After waiting so long for this to come out, I was left underwhelmed after watching it. Then as I thought more about it I became angry. I felt like my childhood had been violated. What we got was anything but this. Rian completely ignored everything JJ. set up in the previous installment, it was akin to him taking a big steaming dump on J.J.'s work whilst giving the middle finger to all the Star Wars fans. He completely ruined the legacy of Luke Skywalker, so much so, that even Mark Hamill now refers to him as Jake Skywalker. Then there was the horrible, incoherent script, unecessary humour, Mary Poppins Leia, unnecessary characters (Rose, & the magenta-haired witch) cut & paste final battle scene, & no actual lightsabre dual involving Luke.

All in all, this is a film any true Star Wars fan should avoid if they want their fond memories of the franchise to remain intact. Rian, you had so much to work with. Why?

The trailers have been phenomenal, they got director Rian Johnson to make the movie, and Rey receives her training from Luke Skywalker in this movie. I walked out, feeling like I have been trolled. What I mean by this is that the movie would show glimpses of answering some of our greatest questions that we had after the force awakens, and then would simply shut it down with answer that makes me feel like I wasted my time. Not to mention that the movie in most of its runtime moves at a snail's pace, and when at this pace, it doesn't really pick itself back up. And plus, the movie just goes on for way too long. After everything went down by like the two hour mark I was kind of okay with, but the last half an hour throws this movie in the dirt. There are some ridiculous moments that take place during the second last act that they have and it actually made me angry, the illogic surrounding this film is astounding and it made me want to leave the theater. What really sucks about this movie is the wasted potential too, because there are some moments in this movie where I look at the movie and I just say too myself, "That could have been done better." The Last Jedi in my opinion is actually worse than the phantom menace and the only reason why I gave it two stars is that there are three moments in the movie where I actually enjoyed myself. The rest of the movie though is stupid and illogical and I hope JJ Abrams does good with Episode Nine, otherwise, I might be done with this new trilogy.

title: 27 Reasons why this movie FAILED. Overall Theme = It makes no sense!
review:
My problems

There's 27 main problems I have and there's probably more. https://tt.amazon.com/0141457590 1) The joke at the start with Poe and hux. Immediately all tension is gone and it took so long. Came across quite annoying. 2) Never liked how Poe went in seemingly alone to take out the Dreadnought cannons which is so stupid because it amazes me that they couldn't take Poe down. He then says "Okay Commander or captain, whatever you like to call me, I just want to know what's going on?". You're impulsive, dangerous, and the last thing we need right now. So stick to your post...and follow my orders". It made no sense to not just tell the guy that you think is dangerous, the plan. He ends up creating a mutiny because what other choice does he have if he thinks they're all going to die. It also leads to the completely useless subplot story of Finn and Rose. The whole thing was essentially put in there to shame him of his "toxic masculinity". It was basically a message to a Han Solo type character, who is a "flyboy" himself. Han "Flyboy" Solo did save the galaxy. 11) Finn and Rose can't act together. They're terrible finishing each others sentences. How they come up with the tracking idea is poor. 12) Then Rey learns the force way too quickly and she's all powerful pretty much. She gets tempted by the dark side and actually willingly goes in but she's not tempted at all. It's just madness really. 13) Then we have the rich people are evil narrative which is done many times across many movies. It's funny because what they showed can also be said about Hollywood. 14) Next we have Rey who is able to wield a lightsaber like she's been doing it for decades. It makes no sense. For someone that thought the Jedi were a myth a week ago, she's really picked it up quick. 15) They meet Del Toro in prison that could have escaped at any time but doesn't for some reason. He just happens to stay there until the exact moment they arrive. I hate convient stuff like that. 16) They show slavery and animal abuse and in the end lets the animals free but leaves the slave children there. No sense to me especially when she says it's worth it now. Also they get arrested for parking violation. Just awful writing. 17) They then show how Luke tried to murder his own nephew which makes no sense to Luke's character. They want us to believe that the man that saw a glimmer of hope in Darth Vader decided to kill Kylo rather than save him. Luke risked his life to save Vader. He believed in him and family. He saw the good in people rather than the evil. That is the whole point of Star Wars. However, now he just has a dream of dark tendencies in Kylo Ren (tendencies that Luke himself had) and decides the best cause of action is to kill a kid going through puberty. Where is the logic in that? It's completely butchered the storyline of Star Wars and mainly Luke Skywalker's character. Luke would never do this. 18) Then Rey goes to the dark pit on the island, falls in and nothing happens. She doesn't turn bad at all. Completely useless pit. I guess all it does it start the idea that she's a nobody in terms of heritage. 19) Then in one of the most annoying scenes, Luke catches Rey and Kylo having a late night facetime call and like a parent comes in and ends the call. He tells her to get off his island and walks away like a parent telling their child to go to bed because you're grounded. Then the most infuriating thing happened. Rey manages to get her staff and strike Luke with it. She managed to hit Luke Skywalker, a man so in touch with the force that he can sense danger miles away. However for some reason, he cannot detect a staff moving at a dangerous pace towards his head. It's unbelievable. What's worse is he's knocked down with Rey towering over him with her spear like she has dominated him. He then grabs a staff using the force and battles and you're thinking she's going to learn a huge lesson here now. Unbelievably though, Rey manages to call Luke's own lightsaber to her and activates it. Now she's towering over Luke Skywalker as if she's about to strike him down and Luke is there with an afraid look on his face. It's unbelievable how weak Luke has become. He loses to Rey in combat and she has only had 2 lessons out of 3. It's truly remarkable. The most idiotic thing I've ever seen in a star wars movie and Leia's space thing was in the same movie. 20) Yoda then blows up the ancient texts and says that Rey already knows what's in those books. Erm...what's the point of having those books then because Rey thought the Jedi were a myth a week ago. She didn't learnt the force in one week surely. And another thing is how Yoda is able to just blow the texts up with a lightning bolt. It would be great if he could have just done that against the tracking system so the resistance could get away. Again these introductions of powers just make no sense. 21) The entire Snoke death is stupid. We know nothing about him. And a guy that was so powerful couldn't sense a lightsaber next to him turning. What a joke. 22) Suicide ships shouldn't be a thing. If that was the case, why not use that against a star destroyer? The reason you can''t is because the shields would have disintegrated the ship surely. 23) All the stormtroopers around Finn and Rose are knocked out. Rose is already up after the suicide ship scene and she drags Finn. There isn't a single cut or mark on either Finn or Rose. Then Finn kills Phasma, who knows if she survives this time. Phasma gets distracted because her other stormtroopers can't manage to kill rose...a mechanic. Dreadful writing. 24) Finn tries to play hero on the rebel base and Rose crashes into him. Forget how she ruined a potentially decent moment, they end up falling right in front of the First Order. However somehow they managed to run back together after surviving a crash without the First Order shooting them. Again just pathetic. It's so ludicrous. Then comes the worst kiss I've seen in a movie. I mean Wow was that awkward. My mate in the cinema kept laughing and continued laughing throughout the movie whenever Finn came on the screen. It was so bad. 25) You then think Luke comes to save the day, flown in on his X-wing. Nope. He force projects himself and hardly fights Kylo Ren. Then when he does his job, he dies of exhaustion. And then he's holding a blue lightsaber which was just destroyed. Luke doesn't fight, he just dodges. Such a bad ending. 26) Rey can lift multiple rocks with her extensive training. I just give up with this movie. 27) Rey talking with Leia about Luke being gone and that it wasn't sad but that it was "peace and purpose" was annoying since it was far from the truth. It was insignificant and insulting actually. Terrible end to an iconic character.

I originally gave it a 5/10 but I was being way too kind after watching it again. It deserves a 4/10.

title: A flawed movie which has its moments
review:
First of all, I must thank all the people leaving 1 or 2 star reviews here. You set my expectations so low, I actually enjoyed The Last Jedi.

TLJ is a deeply flawed film in its basic premise (Luke's character and his rationale), but it is not as bad as most people are making it out to be. IMO its a marked improvement on The Force Awakens, at least it takes some risks and gives us something new, which this franchise so badly needed. The CGI is beautiful and not overdone, the fight sequences are great to watch, and it is not as predictable as its predecessor (TFA was just a poor rehash of ANH).

Here is my take on all the criticisms being leveled at this movie:

1. Luke's rationale: On this one, I agree with all the criticisms. Luke's character was poorly written, his reasoning for leaving everything and not helping the resistance did not make sense at all. His (lack of) reaction to re Hans death did not make sense - surely that should have had more impact that a few words from Yoda. Basically they turned Luke into a grumpy, emotionless shell of a man he used to be, and the reasons for that transformation did not make sense. Almost feels like the writers did not study Luke's character from the original trilogy. Since this is the basic premise on which this story is built, it all falls a bit flat. This is the reason why I have given the movie a 6 rating instead of the 8 or 9 it otherwise would have deserved.

2. Different Force interpretations: Luke projecting himself, Leia's space walk, Spoke moving people from great distance, and Rey doing great things without training.... Most of these are small loopholes. The first two I have no problems with, they are actually new cool things you could do with the force. The concept of how you can use the force has always been quite fluid. The fact that Luke dies from doing what he did made it ok - that explains why Jedi don't do this often. I have issues about the Spoke bit, because it raises so many questions of why the Jedi/Sith need to physically travel at all. The bit about Rey, that is a blunder that was the legacy of TFA, this movie is just picking it up from there.

3. Rey's backstory: I have to give the writer credit here, this was actually refreshing. They took a very big risk here, but the fact that Rey was not related to anyone (Luke, Ben, etc) is awesome. Not all great Jedi need to be born to Jedi. The writers did miss an opportunity not to develop some connection between Rey's abandonment as a child and the resistance that TFA hinted at, but apart from that I have no issues with this. The fans are over-reacting because their fan-theories did not work out. But if we criticized TFA for not taking any risks or giving us anything different, we must praise TLJ for taking such risks.

4. Snoke's death: Again, I have no issues with how Snoke dies. Like the above point, this is a refreshing change - it would have been sad if they had stuck with rehashing of the original trilogy with Rey as Luke, Snoke as the Emperor and Kylo as Vader. After TFA, that was what I was dreading. Instead, we had Snoke showing overconfidence about his complete read of Kylo's mind and dying because of it. I can only commend the writers for taking such a risk with the conventional storyline.

The other criticisms are nitpicking. Yes, the Rose character was poorly developed, as was DJ, and that sub-plot did not add much to the storyline - but not all subplots have to. Yes, the bomber droping bombs in space did not make much sense - if it was a magnetic pull thing, the bomber should not need to travel on top of the destroyer. But those are small things, more than made up for by some great visuals.

Overall, a much better effort that TFA. I can only hope they build on this and continue to take some risks - that is the only way Stars Wars will create a new audience and start a new legacy.

title: A movie of two halves
review: Just returned from viewing this movie in Imax and don't yet know what to make of it. Firstly, it's long. Far, far too long. The movie, and the viewers appreciation of it, would've been greatly improved had it been cut by 45minutes - the first 45minutes. At no time could I truthfully say that I had a clue as to what was going on: the plot is such a mess. Not helped by the Rose character's speech being totally incomprehensible, a common problem with Asian Americans (try making sense of Lucy Liu in the otherwise excellent Elementary). Chewbacca (this passes the spellchecker!) is supposed to be incomprehensible, but then, he's a Wooky, not a human. And all those pointless cute little critters that'll scare most children, what's all that about? Aimed at pre-adolescents, there are sufficiently numerous explosions to keep most interested at least during the performance but don't expect this cash cow to become a classic. A generous 5/10 as the music, coffee and nachos were very good.

title: Consider the Star Wars saga to have ended with Return of the Jedi
review:
The Last Jedi is a spectacular visual film but in term of living up to the awe inspiring Star Wars mythology Rian Johnson failed dismally particularly because he didn't try.

Star Wars has been a part of pop culture for the last 40 years and as I tell my not so enthusiastic wife I know it's not real but it's so much fun to immerse yourself into the fantasy and culture.

The Force Awakens raised some interesting questions that fans were left to ponder and have fun debating...

Who is Snoke and where did he come from? How did he get control of The First Order? Who were Rey's parents? What happened to Luke?

Rian Johnons answers to all of these questions were simply that they don't matter.

It's all about Kylo Ren who has nowhere near the power and presence of Palpatine, Vader or Snoke and is nowhere near as capable of finishing what his grandfather "started".

It was so sad to see Snoke and Phasma (who had her own origin book) stuffed out like flies and the hero of the original trilogy reduced to a bitter old man who contemplated killing his own nephew. Perhaps he was influenced through the force by Snoke to help turn Ben Solo to the Dark side but Rian Johnson will probably tell as that it also doesn't matter.

Rian Johnson should not be allowed near a Star Wars script again and my advice to die hard Star Wars fans is to see it, enjoy it and buy it to add to your collection, but consider the Star Wars saga to have ended with Return Of The Jedi.
